findings.title: update-profile always sends is_interested_in_pass=false, so any profile edit flips the user's Pass interest off
findings.evidence: Boolean inputs are registered as store_true, so an absent flag arrives as False, never None. account.py:238-239 keeps every field that is not None, so is_interested_in_pass=False always survives. Offline probe through cli.main (network blocked, temp CITYMAPPER_ROOT): `update-profile --first-name Ada --dry-run` printed body {"first_name": "Ada", "is_interested_in_pass": false}; `update-profile --last-name Lovelace --dry-run` printed {"last_name": "Lovelace", "is_interested_in_pass": false}. The flag cannot express 'leave unchanged' or an explicit false. tests/test_writes.py:35 calls the function with a dict {"first_name": "Ada"} and skips argparse, which is why 372 tests pass.
findings.proposed_fix: In add_property, register booleans with action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction and default=None, so an absent flag is None, --interested-in-pass is True and --no-interested-in-pass is False. All other boolean reads (dry_run, yes, with_paths, step_free, refresh, exact) use truthiness, so None behaves like False for them. Add a CLI-level test that parses `update-profile --first-name Ada --dry-run` and asserts that the body has only first_name. Break the fix, watch it go red, then restore.
findings.expected_effect: The update-profile body has exactly the fields the user passed (1 of 1 instead of 2). A first-name edit no longer clears Pass interest, and the user can set it to false on purpose.
findings.verify_note: The anchor is at cli.py:24, not 26. Through cli.main with the network blocked, `update-profile --first-name Ada --dry-run` printed body {"first_name": "Ada", "is_interested_in_pass": false}, and the --last-name run also carried is_interested_in_pass false.
findings.outcome_reason: Confirmed at cli.py:24, where booleans used action="store_true", so an absent --interested-in-pass parsed as False and update_profile sent is_interested_in_pass=false. Booleans are now registered with argparse.BooleanOptionalAction and default=None: an absent flag is None, --interested-in-pass is True, --no-interested-in-pass is False. Every other boolean read (dry_run, yes, with_paths, step_free, refresh, exact, stdin) is a truthiness check, so None behaves like False. Side effect: every boolean now also accepts a --no-<name> form, such as --no-dry-run. Existing flags are unchanged.

findings.title: GET-based approval writes (share-journey, create-go-link) are auto-retried up to 3 sends with no new approval
findings.evidence: Transport.send decides retries by HTTP method only. CREATE_TRIP_URL and CREATE_SHORT_URL (endpoints.py:84-85) are GET, and they create public links that cannot be deleted (schemas.json confirmation: 'Visible to anyone with the link; no delete exists'). Offline probe: a fake client raising httpx.ReadTimeout (the request may already have reached the server) made the createtripurl and createshorturl writes go out 3 times each, with sleeps of 5 s and 10 s between them. The POST city-vote went out once. The SKILL error table also says 'The program already retried' and 'resend only with fresh approval', so the retry breaks the approval rule for these two commands.
findings.proposed_fix: Mark write endpoints explicitly, for example `is_write: bool = False` on Endpoint, set True on CREATE_TRIP_URL, CREATE_SHORT_URL, CITY_VOTE and every identity and turnstile write. Then use `can_retry = request.endpoint.method == "GET" and not request.endpoint.is_write` in Transport.send. Add a test in test_transport.py that runs a fake client raising ReadTimeout and asserts one send for every write endpoint.
findings.expected_effect: Each approved write is sent once, not up to 3 times. This rules out duplicate public trip or go links after a timeout and brings the program in line with the SKILL exit-16 guidance.
findings.verify_note: This duplicates stability-1 (GET writes retried up to 3 times at transport.py:108). It names the same line and anchor and gives the same probe result.

findings.title: Approved public-link writes sent over GET are resent up to 3 times on a timeout
findings.evidence: Retry eligibility is decided by HTTP method alone. share-journey (CREATE_TRIP_URL, endpoints.py:84) and create-go-link (CREATE_SHORT_URL, endpoints.py:85) are writes that publish a public link but use GET, and perform_write_public (sharing.py:39) passes them straight to transport.send. Offline probe with httpx.MockTransport raising ReadTimeout: createshorturl GET sends 3, sleeps [5, 10]; createtripurl GET sends 3, sleeps [5, 10]; city-vote POST sends 1. A read timeout after the server already created the link therefore creates up to 2 extra public links from one approval. That contradicts SKILL.md line 112, which says after a write the user should re-read state and resend only with fresh approval. No test covers a GET write.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `writes: bool = False` field to Endpoint and set it on CREATE_TRIP_URL and CREATE_SHORT_URL (and any other state-changing GET). In Transport.send compute `is_read = request.endpoint.method == "GET" and not request.endpoint.writes` and use it for can_retry. Add a test in tests/test_transport.py asserting one send and no sleeps for a GET write on ReadTimeout.
findings.expected_effect: An approved share-journey or create-go-link reaches the site at most once per approval (3 sends down to 1 on timeout). Read GETs keep the 2 retries.
findings.verify_note: transport.py:108 decides retries by method alone. In my MockTransport ReadTimeout probe, createshorturl and createtripurl were each sent 3 times with sleeps [5, 10], and city-vote was sent once. This is the earliest entry of the issue that scope-1 and safety-1 repeat.
findings.outcome_reason: The defect was still there at transport.py:154: retry eligibility was decided by method alone. I added `writes: bool = False` to Endpoint and set writes=True on CREATE_TRIP_URL and CREATE_SHORT_URL. No new endpoint literal was added. Transport.send now computes `is_read = request.endpoint.method == "GET" and not request.endpoint.writes` and uses it for retries, so read GETs keep their 2 retries.

Offline probe through cli.main with a fake transport: searchpost returning a list -> uncaught AttributeError; routestatus route with status.level null in get-disruptions -> uncaught TypeError from int(None) at lines.py:72; var/cache/catalogue.json containing [] -> uncaught AttributeError at catalogue.py:95; catalogue.json {"fetched_at": now} with no regions -> uncaught KeyError 'regions' at catalogue.py:112. In Catalogue.load and RegionConfigs.get treat a cached value that is not a dict, lacks 'regions'/'config', or has a non-numeric fetched_at as a cache miss so it is refetched instead of raising. Add tests in tests/test_cli.py for a drifted body and in tests/test_commands.py for a [] catalogue cache.

findings.title: live_check never downgrades readiness when a command fails, so help and SKILL.md keep saying "verified live"
findings.evidence: I ran it offline with run_cli and SITE_ROOT/READINESS_FILE pointed at a tempdir, seeded with get-line and get-lines at "verified live". I faked get-line exiting 14 (ContractBroken) and get-lines failing its invariant. The output was "live check: 0 of 2 runs passed" with exit 1, but readiness still held {'status': 'verified live', 'verified_at': 'old'} for both commands. The nonzero-exit branch (lines 224-235) never touches readiness, and the invariant-fail branch uses setdefault, which leaves an existing status in place. Commands with several labels (plan-journey x2, find-nearby x2, get-departures x3) also get overwritten to verified by any later passing label even when an earlier one failed. render_skill.py and registry.readiness_of read this file, so a broken command keeps advertising "verified live" to Claude. None of this is covered: tests/ has no test for live_check.py.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep a per-command failure set during the run. On any failure (nonzero exit, schema or invariant problem) set readiness[command] = {"status": "failing live: <class or first problem>", "checked_at": stamp, "log": ...}. Mark a command "verified live" only if every selected label for it passed in this run. Write readiness in a finally block so a crash mid-run still records what ran. Add tests/test_live_check.py that monkeypatches run_cli, SITE_ROOT and READINESS_FILE and asserts the downgrade. Break the fix, watch the test go red, then restore it.
findings.expected_effect: After a live regression, help and the regenerated SKILL.md show the failing status on the next live_check instead of a stale "verified live". In the case above, 2 of 2 stale statuses get corrected.

Make every write require `--confirm <digest>` together with --yes, and raise UsageError when the recomputed digest differs, showing both requests. Add `confirm` to each write's input_schema in schemas.json. Change the SKILL Writes section so the call the user approves includes `--confirm <digest>` from the dry run.

I confirmed this by reading the code. A live search returning different results between the two runs is plausible, but I did not observe it.
findings.outcome_reason: Request.confirm_digest() is the first 12 hex characters of sha256 over method, url and body. The created, modified and last_used fields are removed first, including inside JSON-string bodies such as save-journey's document_data. findings.evidence: context.py line 91 builds HH:MM as datetime.now(zone).replace(hour, minute) with no rollover. So 'leave at 07:00 tomorrow' passed as `--depart-at 07:00` in the evening plans today's 07:00. The skill presents HH:MM as equivalent to ISO 8601 with no warning. Same path feeds get-stop-schedule --time (departures.py line 188).

Offline probe via cli.main with searchpost returning {"places": [...]}: search-places exits 0 with {"results": []}; plan-journey with the same drift exits 17 NotFound "No place with coordinates matches 'Main St'". The skill maps 17 to 'no such place', so a site change is reported to the user as a bad place name instead of exit 14 ContractBroken.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `response.get("results", [])` with `require_list(response, "results", "search response")` (import from .models). Add a test in tests/test_commands.py that a searchpost body without 'results' raises ContractBroken for search-places and plan-journey.
findings.expected_effect: Search shape drift exits 14 ContractBroken for all 7 commands that resolve text places, instead of exit 0 with no results or a misleading exit 17.
findings.verify_note: context.py:120 reads response.get("results", []). With a fake transport returning {"places": [...]}, search() returned [] and Context.place raised NotFound (exit 17), not ContractBroken (14). I lowered the severity because this only happens when the site changes shape, not in normal use.
findings.outcome_reason: Agent reverted it for lack of test_cli.py access; applied in the main session: search results use require_list; the shape-drift CLI test asserts detail.field == 'results' for search cases and gains two cases. Bite: old line gave '3 failed, 1 passed', fix '4 passed'.

findings.title: Unreadable pacer state locks every command out forever while promising 900 seconds
findings.evidence: _load_state rebuilds the fail-closed halt from the current clock on every read and never writes it, and turn() raises in _raise_if_halted before the try/finally that would rewrite the file. Offline probe with var/state/pacer.json = '{not json' and an injected clock: after +0 s, +1000 s and +86400 s each turn() raised RateLimited 'stays stopped for 900 more seconds'; the file stayed '{not json'; status() reported seconds_remaining 900. Every site command then exits 12, and SKILL.md line 108 tells the user to wait, which never helps. Fail-closed is right; the endless sliding window and false countdown are the defect.
findings.proposed_fix: When the file is unreadable, persist the fail-closed halt once: inside the lock, write {"last_request_at": now, "halted_until": now + HALT_SECONDS_AFTER_THROTTLE, "halt_reason": UNREADABLE_REASON} over the bad file (use _write_state), then return it, so the halt expires after 900 s as stated. Add a test in tests/test_pacing.py that a corrupt file halts, then allows a turn after the clock passes 900 s.
findings.expected_effect: A torn or hand-edited pacer.json costs one 15-minute halt instead of an indefinite lockout of all commands, and the reported seconds_remaining counts down.
findings.verify_note: pacing.py:41 returns a fresh halt at clock()+900 on every read of an unreadable file. turn() raises in _raise_if_halted before the try/finally that would rewrite it, so the halt slides forever while status reports 900 s left.
findings.outcome_reason: The defect held: _load_state built a fresh clock()+900 halt on every read of an unreadable file and never saved it. _load_state now takes persist_unreadable. turn() (on entry and in finally) and halt() pass True while holding the lock, so the fail-closed halt is written once with _write_state and expires after 900 s. status() still reads without the lock and does not write, so before the first turn it reports 900 s, and afterwards it counts down from the saved halt. Pacing defaults are unchanged.

findings.title: 200 error envelope detection misses bodies with 4+ keys or a boolean error
findings.anchor: has_error_envelope = isinstance(body, dict) and isinstance(body.get("error"), (str, dict)) and len(body) <= 3
findings.evidence: Offline probe of classify(200, application/json, ...): {"error": "Invalid region", "code": 400, "message": "x", "details": {}} is returned as a success body; {"error": true, "message": "bad"} is returned as a success body. The site's own bundle (research/bundle/bundle.js) rejects any response with a truthy error: `t&&!t.error?e(t):n(new Error(t&&t.error||...))`. None of the 33 JSON fixtures in tests/fixtures has a top-level 'error' key, so widening the check does not reclassify any recorded success. The len(body) <= 3 cutoff is arbitrary, and a missed envelope then surfaces as an uncaught KeyError or a silent empty result downstream.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the condition to `isinstance(body, dict) and bool(body.get("error"))` and keep the per-item 'error' handling in get-journey-times untouched since it is nested. Add tests in tests/test_classify.py for a 4-key envelope and for error: true.
findings.expected_effect: Both probed envelope shapes raise ApiError (exit 13) instead of passing as data; all 372 existing tests should still pass because no fixture carries a top-level error.
findings.verify_note: classify.py:49 has the anchor. classify(200, json) returned both probe bodies as success: the 4-key error envelope and {error: true}. The bundle contains `t&&!t.error?e(t):n(new Error(t&&t.error`. None of the 31 JSON fixtures has a top-level error key, so the stricter check does not reclassify any recorded success.
findings.outcome_reason: The defect held at classify.py:49. The condition is now split into is_object and has_error_envelope = is_object and bool(body.get("error")), which matches the bundle's truthy-error rule. Nested per-item errors are untouched. No test file other than test_classify.py has a top-level error body. tests/test_classify.py: '29 passed in 0.03s'. tests/test_transport.py with tests/test_times.py: '25 passed in 0.17s'. Behaviour change: a body with error set to an empty string now passes as data where it used to raise.

findings.title: The skill says to report live values with their fetch time, but no live command outputs one, and bus departures return updated: null
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:90 (rendered from render_skill.py:93) says "Live transit values change on every call; report them with the time they were fetched." The only output with fetched_at is list-cities, and that value is the catalogue cache time. get-departures returns seconds_away relative to an unstated instant. For bus feeds, updated is hard-coded to None (departures.py:100) because the real /api/1/departures body has no last_updated_time: I checked var/captures/run-2026-10-10-082844-stop-nyc-bus.jsonl and the replay captures. plan-journey, get-journey-times and get-vehicles have no timestamp field in their output schemas either. Claude has to make up the time from its own clock.
findings.proposed_fix: In cli.main, after command.function returns a dict for a non-local command, add "fetched_at": the UTC ISO time taken just before the first request (Transport can record it at the first send). In get_departures, fall back to that time when the feed gives no last_updated_time. Add fetched_at to each read output_schema through plan.json and sync_schemas.py, and assert it in test_read_output_matches_its_schema.
findings.expected_effect: All 28 verified-live read commands carry a machine-readable fetch time, so the instruction at SKILL.md:90 can be followed without guessing. Bus departure output goes from updated: null to a concrete time.
findings.verify_note: departures.py:100 returns None for updated, and the only fetched_at in any output is list-cities' catalogue cache time. The single last_updated_time in the nyc bus capture comes from /api/2/nearby, not departures. The agent can use its own clock as an approximation, so I lowered the severity.
findings.outcome_reason: Confirmed departures.py:100 returns None for the bus feed and that no live read emitted a fetch time. transport.py: added utc_now_iso() (ISO 8601 UTC with Z) and an injectable clock. Transport records first_sent_at (set once, just before the first request after the pacer wait) and last_sent_at. cli.py: new run_command(command, context, values), used by main. For a remote read (kind read, live_policy not local) that sent at least one request, it adds fetched_at = first_sent_at with setdefault. findings.title: get-line-status and get-disruptions fetch the identical routestatus response separately
